title: Pay-period statements with bonuses and a platform fee
scenario: Per-task pay inside a half-open pay period plus spreadsheet-exported bonuses, minus a 2.5% fee rounded half-up, with a minimum payout that decides paid vs carried over.

verified.why_correct: Multiplying a Decimal after quantize looks like it could leave fractions, but quantize to 0.01 guarantees a whole number of cents, it rounds half up as the spec says, and it strips `$` and thousands separators. Blank amounts return None so the loader can skip them.

bugs.title: Period end treated as inclusive
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_1_base_earnings: C-01 base_cents is 860 instead of 650 (T-107, a 210-cent transcribe task at exactly 2026-04-15 00:00, is paid). Every other contributor matches.
bugs.why: The period is half-open. T-107 was completed at exactly 2026-04-15 00:00, which is the next period's start, so it must not be paid now.
hints: C-01 is overpaid by exactly one transcribe task. Which one?
Look at T-107's timestamp and the period end in period.json.
in_period uses `<= end`; README rule 2 says `< end`.
probes: Why is T-101 (exactly at start) still paid?
What would go wrong across two consecutive periods if both ends were inclusive?

bugs.title: Byte order mark kept in the first header
bugs.old: with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
bugs.new: with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_2_bonuses: every bonus_cents is 0 and C-08/C-09 disappear from the statement entirely; task earnings are unaffected.
bugs.why: bonuses.csv starts with a UTF-8 BOM. Read as plain utf-8, the first header becomes '\ufeffcontributor_id' (strip() does not remove it), so `r.get("contributor_id")` is None and every bonus row is skipped as having no id.
hints: Every bonus is 0 and C-08/C-09 are missing. Is bonuses.csv being read at all?
Print the keys of the first row the loader yields for bonuses.csv.
probes: Why did tasks.csv and rates.csv load fine through the same helper?
Why didn't this raise a KeyError?

bugs.title: Fee rounded with banker's rounding
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_3_fees_on_task_only_earners: C-03 shows (26, 1034) instead of (27, 1033) and C-05 (30, 1190) instead of (31, 1189). C-04 is unchanged.
bugs.why: Python's round() rounds halves to the even neighbour, so 26.5 → 26 and 30.5 → 30. The spec rounds halves up.
hints: C-03's fee is 26 but 1060 × 2.5% is 26.5. What rule decides that?
round() is half-to-even; use integer half-up: (gross * 250 + 5000) // 10000.
probes: Why was C-04's fee (8.125) right either way?
Why does doing the arithmetic in integer cents avoid float surprises?

context_qa.a: For each CSV data row it yields a dict whose keys are the header names passed through clean() and lower-cased; values are the raw strings. It is used for rates, tasks and bonuses.

context_qa.q: How does base_earnings decide whether a task is paid?
context_qa.a: It skips task ids it has already seen, then skips tasks whose status isn't `approved` or whose type isn't in the rates table, then checks `in_period(completed_at, period)`. Paid tasks add their rate in cents to the contributor's total.

context_qa.q: What do the period values look like after load_period?
context_qa.a: `start` and `end` are datetimes (bare dates become midnight), `fee_percent` is a float (2.5), and `min_payout_cents` is an int (2000).
The union of contributor ids with task earnings and ids with bonuses, sorted. A contributor with only bonuses gets base_cents 0.

context_qa.q: How does to_cents handle '$1,000.00' or a blank?
context_qa.a: It strips `$` and commas, returns None for a blank string, otherwise quantizes the Decimal to 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_UP and multiplies by 100, returning an int.

context_qa.q: What does platform_fee return for a given gross?
context_qa.a: An int number of cents computed from gross_cents and fee_percent; build_statement subtracts it from gross to get net.
